historicalReferences: While the main Interlagos circuit has seen countless battles, the Kart Circuit has nurtured generations of Brazilian talent, many finding their feet here.
Senna, Fittipaldi, Piquet – all honed their skills on tracks just like this one. The Kart Circuit is a breeding ground for Brazilian motorsport legends.
It's impossible to be at Interlagos without thinking of Senna. His spirit lives on, inspiring these young karters to push themselves to the limit.
Many current F1 drivers started their careers right here on this kart circuit, proving its importance as a stepping stone.
The Kart Circuit has witnessed its fair share of dramatic finishes and championship deciders over the years, albeit on a smaller scale.
While the main circuit is known for its incredible overtakes, this Kart Circuit has seen some equally daring moves, just in miniature.
This Kart Circuit has been a training ground for countless Brazilian racing stars, fostering a legacy of speed and skill.
Think of this Kart Circuit as a mini-Interlagos, a place where future champions learn the fundamentals of racing.
It's a different kind of history here on the Kart Circuit, a history of development, of learning, and of chasing dreams.
While the Grand Prix track holds the glory, this Kart Circuit is where the foundations are laid, the first steps taken on the road to F1.
cornerCallouts: Drivers will need to brake hard into Turn 1, setting up for a clean exit and run down to Turn 2.
The key to a good lap here is carrying momentum through the esses at Turn 3 and Turn 4.
Turn 5 is a deceptively tricky corner, demanding precision and a delicate touch on the throttle.
Watch out for drivers trying to make a move into Turn 7, a potential overtaking spot.
The long, sweeping Turn 8 is all about maintaining speed and maximizing grip.
Turn 10 offers a chance for a late divebomb, but drivers must be careful not to overshoot the corner.
Exiting Turn 11 cleanly is crucial for setting up a good run onto the final straight.
The final corner, Turn 12, is a tight hairpin that demands precision and commitment.
strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a factor, even on this short Kart Circuit. Managing the rubber will be key to a strong finish.
With such a short lap, every tenth of a second counts. Precision and consistency are paramount.
Fuel load isn't as critical here as on the full circuit, but drivers still need to manage their consumption effectively.
The slipstream effect is amplified on this Kart Circuit, making tactical drafting essential for overtaking.
The pit window is relatively short, so teams need to execute quick and efficient pit stops.
Track position is crucial on this tight and twisty circuit. Overtaking can be difficult, so qualifying well is vital.
With frequent changes in direction, kart setup will be critical to ensure optimal balance and grip.
Maintaining momentum is key on this flowing circuit. Drivers need to avoid scrubbing off speed in the corners.
weatherCommentary: The weather in São Paulo can be unpredictable. A sudden downpour could quickly turn this race on its head.
The humidity here can be oppressive, especially in the afternoon. Drivers will need to stay hydrated and manage their energy levels.
The altitude of Interlagos can also affect engine performance. Teams need to adjust their settings accordingly.
There's a chance of thunderstorms later today. Keep an eye on the skies; the race could be affected.
The wind can be a factor here, especially on the exposed sections of the circuit. Drivers will need to adjust their lines accordingly.
